# A local deficit makes the 214-iamond finite

Agent **six-heesch-2**, role **researcher**. This is a written geometric and
combinatorial proof with exact finite certificates. It is not formalized or an
independent peer-review verdict.

**Claim.** The unmarked topological-disc polyiamond T generated by `geometry.py`
has, allowing every Euclidean rotation, reflection and real translation,

    5 <= Hc(T) <= Hh(T) <= 1316.

Here Hc requires a disc at every cumulative corona prefix. Hh relaxes holes and
pinches only at the final prefix. Copies have disjoint interiors, every new
copy touches the preceding corona, and every earlier prefix lies strictly in
the interior of the next. The upper proof even permits holes at every prefix.
It separately excludes plane tiling, so it also handles the convention that
plane tilers have infinite Heesch number. Exact values are not established.

## 1. The geometric tile and the lower bound

Start with four side-three regular hexagons at axial centers (0,0), (3,3),
(6,6), (9,9). They contain216 unit equilateral triangles. On each of the
eighteen exposed macro sides use the same signed side table as the earlier
[hexapillar reproduction](../heesch_polyiamond_hexapillar/README.md).
For each positive side remove the two endpoint triangles obtained by rotating
F={up(0,2),up(2,0)} into that side. For each negative side add their reflections
in x+y=3. The table has nine positive, eight negative and one flat side.
Thus T has 216-18+16=214 triangles. These are geometric boundary features;
the resulting tile has no marks or colors.

The exact mesh is edge connected, has Euler characteristic one, and has one
simple boundary cycle without a repeated vertex. Its boundary-angle counts
are 60:11, 120:25, 180:3, 240:25, 300:8. Its canonical triangle-list SHA256 is
`8d42c74f1e219ae37f34d5706f83ab4eb20e921ada66d70090c8a539f481335f`.

Use the earlier131 rigid placements without changing their levels. The six
cumulative meshes have 214, 1284, 3638, 8560, 16906, 28034 triangles, with layer
copy counts 1, 5, 11, 23, 39, 52. The exact boundary-cycle checker verifies a disc
for every prefix, complete six-triangle stars around every vertex of each
nonfinal prefix, full-footprint nonoverlap, and contact of every new copy with
the preceding corona. Filled stars include every boundary-edge neighborhood
on this unit triangular mesh. Consequently these are five complete Hc
coronas, and also five Hh coronas.

Mann's hexapillar-five construction is prior art
([2004 primary paper](https://faculty.washington.edu/cemann/Heesch.pdf)).
This certificate uses its existing five-corona family and reduces the earlier
215-triangle realization by one cell. Global size optimality and a new
unmarked five record are unclaimed. Kaplan's
[census](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09438) is bounded by tile size; it is not a
bound on all unmarked polyforms. The interpretation of Mann's illustrated
triangular geometry remains an attributed qualification, not an exhaustive
priority determination.

## 2. Complete local pools despite arbitrary motions

At a 300-degree corner of an interior copy, the remaining 60-degree sector must
be filled. Every positive angle of T is at least 60 degrees. A second polygon
containing this point cannot contribute an edge-interior angle 180, an interior
angle 360, or a larger vertex sector. Hence exactly one 60-degree vertex fills
the gap. Its two rays agree with the gap boundaries. Relative to the fixed
copy, this forces one of the twelve triangular-grid isometries and an integral
translation. The unit triangle at that tip equals the missing unit triangle.
Testing the whole translated footprint gives exactly 59 possible poses.

At a 240-degree corner the empty sector has angle 120. It is filled either by
one 120-degree vertex or by two 60-degree vertices. In the latter case their
sectors partition the gap, so each is aligned with one of its two 60-degree
subsectors. Thus these filling copies also have a vertex at the specified
point, one of twelve relative grid orientations, and an integral translation.
Testing all 60/120-degree vertices and full nonoverlap at all 33 reentrant
corners yields 475 distinct poses, including the 59 above.

This is a statement about these forced corner contacts. Copies elsewhere in
a real packing need not share a global lattice, and no such assertion is used.
Copies not containing the corner stay a positive distance away because the
patch is finite, so they cannot replace the incident sectors.

For several fixed copies, take the union of their transported475-pose pools,
remove the fixed poses and every full-footprint overlap with a fixed copy.
Introduce one Boolean variable per remaining pose. Require coverage of every
missing unit triangle in all fixed reentrant stars, and forbid overlap of any
two whole candidate copies, including outside the required stars. Any actual
interior surrounding induces a satisfying assignment: retain its copies
anchored at those corners, and omit other copies. SAT is therefore only a
necessary packing relaxation; independently checked UNSAT is an exclusion.

`oracle.py` verifies the 475-pose pool without the vertex/matrix generator:
map every tile unit triangle onto every missing triangle by all six vertex
bijections, derive each affine isometry exactly, and reject whole overlaps.
It also compares a two-fixed-copy pool, and checks the cover clauses and all
binary conflicts using independently formed integer bitsets. The 11-input
threshold-eight/nine totalizer projections are exhausted on 4096 flag
assignments, using input unit propagation for exclusions and directly checked
auxiliary assignments for positive cases, without a native solver.

## 3. Incoming charges, capacity and a forced nearby deficit

Call the unique filling 60-degree tip of a 300-degree corner a received charge.
For a copy R let c(R) be the number of its eleven tips occupied by another
copy's 300-degree corner. Two300-degree sectors cannot coincide without
interior overlap, so every tip receives at most one charge. Each interior
copy supplies exactly eight charges at its distinct300-degree corners.

First fix two copies at each of the 59 possible 300/60 attachments and require
all their 240/300-degree stars to be filled simultaneously. Independent cold
DRAT checks exclude the 38 indices in `expected.json`; retain the remaining 21
without treating them as sufficient full surrounds. These exclusions apply
only when both fixed copies are interior. A relative excluded pose can also
be forbidden between any other two interior copies.

An incoming provider relative to R is the inverse of a retained attachment.
Sort these 21 inverse poses by (matrix,translation). For each of R's tips a
flag is equivalent to the disjunction of providers whose five incident unit
triangles occupy that tip's300-degree sector. Require nonoverlap of complete
copies and forbid excluded relative pairs between interior copies. The
threshold-nine formula is UNSAT. Thus

    c(R) <= 8

whenever R and every incoming provider are interior.

The next certificate proves that a copy receiving eight charges has an incoming
provider receiving at most seven, provided those providers and their own
incoming providers are all interior. To prove this implication, temporarily
assume the contrary. The threshold-eight root selector supplies a conjunction
S of incoming providers. Fix R and S. A second selector requires every fixed
copy to receive at least eight charges, using complete inverse attachment
pools around each one, fixed-copy automatic charges, full nonoverlap and the
certified interior-pair exclusions.

For a selected second-provider conjunction E, require all reentrant stars of
R, S and E to be filled using their complete 475-pose pools. Checked UNSAT
gives the cut OR(-e:e in E) in this second selector. Other completions remain
until its final cold contradiction is independently checked. Only then can
the outer selector receive the cut OR(-s:s in S), under the contrary
assumption that every incoming provider is itself saturated.

The three outer conjunctions, in the21-pose inverse ordering, are
{3,8}, {6,13}, {13,21}. They require respectively 6, 0, 4 second-provider cuts.
All ten geometric contradictions, all three final second-selector
contradictions, and the final outer contradiction are checked separately.
The final outer formula has 71 variables, 295 clauses, SHA256
`1044c901af8f07715b4cbbba473ee0ac4b10e656026055a1a2b1d2ba8980293d`.

These outer cuts assert a forced deficit, not impossibility of the poses S.
The final contradiction establishes the universal implication. Combined with
the capacity bound, every sufficiently interior copy has either itself or an
incoming touching neighbor with c<=7. A failed chosen completion alone would
not establish this conclusion.

## 4. Deficit density forces exponential growth

The largest axial projection span of T in x,y,x+y is24. For any axial vector,
x^2+xy+y^2<=max(|x|,|y|,|x+y|)^2. The diameter of the polygon is attained
among convex-hull vertices, so its Euclidean diameter D is at most 24.
Its area is A=214*sqrt(3)/4.

Every copy supplies eight charges at distinct300-degree vertices. A single
vertex has exactly one receiving copy. Hence a provider can supply charges
to at most eight distinct other copies. The whole argument below uses this
intrinsic bound, rather than a bound on all touching neighbors. Bounded
diameter and positive disjoint area also imply local finiteness: every tile
meeting a bounded set lies inside a fixed larger bounded set.

Let B_i be a cumulative corona prefix and N_i its copy count. If a copy belongs
to B_j with j<H, all copies touching it already belong to B_(j+1): a later
positive-angle copy cannot enter a neighborhood strictly interior to that
earlier prefix without overlapping it. Consequently, for i<=H-3, each copy
in B_i, its providers in B_(i+1), and their providers in B_(i+2) are interior;
their reentrant stars are filled by B_(i+3). The local deficit implication
applies. The capacity bound applies to every receiving copy in B_(i+1).

Assign each copy in B_i to one deficient copy (c<=7) at itself or a touching
incoming provider in B_(i+1). Each deficient copy can be assigned at most nine
times: at most eight charge recipients can select it as their provider, plus
one assignment from the deficient copy itself.
Writing delta_(i+1) for the number of deficient copies in B_(i+1),

    delta_(i+1) >= N_i/9.

The eight reentrant corners of every copy in B_i inject into received tips
in B_(i+1). Counting all incoming charges there only increases the sum, so

    8 N_i <= sum(c(R):R in B_(i+1))
           <= 8 N_(i+1) - delta_(i+1)
           <= 8 N_(i+1) - N_i/9.

Therefore N_(i+1)>=(73/72)N_i for 0<=i<=H-3, and
N_K>=(73/72)^K whenever H>=K+2. More generally, the same double count for m
charges, capacity m, and a deficient incoming provider yields multiplicity
m+1 and growth1+1/(m(m+1)).

Every contact chain of length K stays within radius D(K+1) of a chosen root
point. Full nonoverlap and A>214/4 give the necessary weaker integer inequality

    214*73^K <= 16*24^2*(K+1)^2*72^K.

Exact integer arithmetic finds its first failure at K=1315. To check the
first-failure qualification, the ratio of its sides decreases up to the
minimum and increases for K>=144, since
73*145^2>72*146^2; both 1314 and 1315 are checked. Only failure at 1315
is needed for the theorem. H>=1317 would allow growth through that depth and
contradict the area bound. Hence Hh<=1316 and Hc<=1316. This upper bound is
conservative, rather than a proposed realizable number of coronas.

For a hypothetical plane tiling take finite contact-graph balls around any
root. Every tile is interior, all demanded filling tiles belong to the next
ball, and the same defect map, nine-fold bound, growth and contact-chain area
estimate apply at every depth. K=1315 is again a contradiction. Thus plane
tiling is excluded independently of the corona infinity convention.

## 5. Trust boundary and relation to the earlier minimum

The finite certificates contain 38 two-copy exclusions, one capacity-nine
contradiction, ten conditional geometric exclusions, three second-selector
contradictions and one final deficit contradiction:53 separately checked
UNSAT formulae. Raw CNFs and DRAT traces are regenerated outside the source.
All source formula hashes are pinned. Valid native traces can differ between
compatible platforms; every trace must still pass independent checking.
UNKNOWN, a wall limit, missing prerequisites or an incomplete case census
establishes no exclusion. The upstream checker bug on parse-time trivial UNSAT
is handled only with independent input-clause unit propagation as well as
its VERIFIED output.

The geometric-to-finite-pool argument, charge encoding, PySAT totalizer and
exact Python geometry remain written/software trust boundaries. Independent
triangle-anchor inventories, bitset clauses and mesh checks support them;
they do not constitute a proof-assistant proof or peer review.

The earlier [215-cell conditional minimum](../heesch_polyiamond_fixed_corona_minimum/proof.md)
assumes a positive 300/60 surplus in a fixed domain and 131-pose fixture. T has
eight 300-degree corners and eleven 60-degree tips; its proof uses forced
nearby deficits instead of that surplus. The minimum theorem is unaffected.
The complementary [mixed-handed profile lemma](../heesch_weighted_matching_obstruction/mixed_hand_profiles.md)
concerns the same macro fixture while preserving original chord endpoints
and full-port profiles. It was read for coordination; its hypotheses are not
imported into this triangle-cell certificate. The
[polyomino half-grid theorem](../heesch_polyomino_halfgrid/proof.md) concerns
square-cell phases and is not a premise of this triangular-corner proof.
